title: Random Processes
intro: A random process is a random quantity that evolves in time. Four models cover most of the ground: Markov chains, random walks and martingales, Poisson processes, and Brownian motion.

items: Markov Chains (#/probability/processes/markov-chains): memoryless random dynamics on a finite or countable set of states, stationary distributions and convergence.
Random Walks and Martingales (#/probability/processes/random-walks-and-martingales): sums of steps, gambler's ruin, fair games and optional stopping.
Poisson Processes (#/probability/processes/poisson-processes): random arrivals in continuous time, and continuous-time Markov chains.
Brownian Motion (#/probability/processes/brownian-motion): the continuous limit of a random walk, and the starting point of stochastic calculus.
J. R. Norris, Markov Chains, Cambridge University Press (1997)
G. R. Grimmett and D. R. Stirzaker, Probability and Random Processes, 4th edition, Oxford University Press (2020), chapters 6 to 13
